input.prompt:
I'm reviewing a Go CLI codebase (repo at /home/daytona/repo, package github.com/entireio/cli). I need to understand what happens when you `git push` to a remote whose URL uses the "entire://" protocol (created via `entire repo mirror use`, see cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_use.go and cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go's mirrorCloneURL function).

Specifically: does a `git push` to an `entire://<cluster-host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>` remote actually forward/proxy the push through to the real upstream GitHub repository (so pushing a commit there is equivalent to pushing to github.com), or does it push into a separate mirror copy hosted on Entire's infrastructure that is NOT automatically synced back to the real GitHub repo (i.e., a divergent copy)?

Look for:
1. A git remote helper implementation (e.g. something registering as `git-remote-entire` or similar) - how does it implement push?
2. Any documentation in docs/architecture/*.md describing mirror push/pull semantics, or "mirror" concept in general.
3. Comments in repo_mirror*.go, repo_clone.go, or gitremote package explaining what "mirror" means and whether it's bidirectionally synced with the origin forge.

I'm trying to determine: if a CLI flow does `git remote set-url origin entire://cluster.example/gh/owner/repo` (replacing the real GitHub origin) and then does `git push origin some-branch`, does that commit end up reachable on the real github.com/owner/repo, or does it just land in Entire's mirror storage without reaching GitHub? Report concisely (under 300 words) with file/line references and quote the key explanatory comments/docs you find.

content.text:
This test-plan doc is about checkpoint sync mechanics generally (not entire:// mirror-to-GitHub sync specifically) — not directly relevant to the question. I have enough evidence now.

Based on the code, I can answer confidently.

## Answer

A push to `entire://<cluster-host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>` lands in Entire's separate mirror storage on that cluster — it does **not** forward to the real GitHub repo, and there is no automatic sync-back.

**1. The remote helper's push path** (`/home/daytona/repo/cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go`): git execs `git-remote-entire`, which builds an HTTP `transport.New(...)` (`internal/remotehelper/transport`) pointed at `nodeCfg := replicas.Resolve(parsedURL)` — the resolved cluster host/replica nodes from the `entire://` URL — and hands that to `githelper.Run`. `gitActionFromRequest` (line 453) classifies requests by path suffix `/git-receive-pack` (push) vs `/git-upload-pack` (pull), both sent to the same cluster transport. There is no code path anywhere in this binary that dials `api.github.com` or `github.com`; every request goes to the Entire cluster's data plane (`entire-server`/`entiredb`, per `docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md`'s table: "Resource: git cluster ... entire-server / entiredb"). So push and pull both terminate at the mirror's storage, not at GitHub.

**2. Mirror creation is a one-time/one-way import, not live sync.** `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go` line 482: `repo mirror create` "registers a mirror placement for that repo on the target cluster, then waits for the initial **GitHub→EntireDB clone** to finish" — a one-way, one-time clone at creation time. Nothing describes GitHub being kept in sync with pushes made to the mirror afterward.

**3. `repo_mirror_use.go`'s own doc comment is explicit that this is local-only and can diverge.** Line ~397-410 (`newRepoMirrorUseCmd` Long text): "Rewrites the local git remote so fetch and push go through an Entire mirror **instead of the forge**... the previous URL is kept as `upstream` so **the forge stays reachable**." That "keep the forge reachable separately" framing, plus preserving the old GitHub URL under a distinct `upstream` remote, only makes sense if the mirror and the forge are two independent stores that a user must explicitly push to separately (`git push upstream` to reach real GitHub).

**Conclusion:** `git remote set-url origin entire://cluster/gh/owner/repo` followed by `git push origin <branch>` writes the commit into the Entire cluster's mirror copy only. It does not become reachable on github.com/owner/repo unless something separately pushes it there (e.g., the user later runs `git push upstream <branch>` against the preserved GitHub remote). The mirror is a divergent copy, not a transparent proxy to GitHub.

1. content.text:
This confirms the git-remote-entire helper simply proxies smart-HTTP git protocol (upload-pack/receive-pack) to the Entire cluster — it's a transport layer to the mirror storage itself, with no GitHub-forwarding logic.

## Findings

I found no code, comment, or doc anywhere in this repo indicating that Entire automatically syncs/mirrors a commit pushed to an entire:// mirror back to GitHub — no webhook receiver, background sync job, or GitHub App push/PR-creation logic exists in this client codebase.

**Evidence of one-way (GitHub → mirror) sync only:**
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:481-483` (`entire repo mirror create` docs): "registers a mirror placement... then waits for the initial **GitHub→EntireDB clone** to finish" — the documented sync direction is explicitly one-way, GitHub into the mirror.
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:450-455`: mirrors are "GitHub-mirror placements" managed on EntireDB clusters — a storage location, not a bidirectional sync target.
- `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:448-467`: the `git-remote-entire` protocol helper only classifies/forwards smart-HTTP `git-receive-pack` (push) and `git-upload-pack` (fetch) requests to the Entire cluster over its own transport — there is no GitHub-forwarding code path.

**What `entire trail` actually does** (`cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:1001-1009,1985-1998`): Creating a trail explicitly pushes the branch to the `origin` remote itself (`pushBranchToOrigin`, line 1004/1006: "push branch %q to origin") — trails do not push anywhere else or create anything on GitHub directly; they just call Entire's own `/api/v1/trails/...` API (`cmd/entire/cli/api/trails.go`) referencing whatever `origin` already holds (mirror or GitHub, whichever `origin` is pointed at). No `gh pr create`/GitHub PR-creation call exists anywhere in the repo (only unrelated `CIWebhook` API types, for CI, not sync). `docs/architecture/*.md` has no file dedicated to trails at all, and none of the existing architecture docs mention "sync back," "forge push," or any GitHub-App-driven mirror-to-GitHub flow.

**Answer:** A commit pushed only to the Entire mirror (never pushed to the real GitHub `upstream`/origin remote) never becomes visible on github.com through any mechanism in this repo. Mirrors are documented and coded as receiving a one-time initial GitHub→mirror clone plus best-effort push fan-out into Entire's own storage; nothing pushes back out to GitHub. Opening a "trail" doesn't change this — it just pushes the branch to whatever `origin` is currently configured to (which, per `repo_mirror_use.go`, could be the mirror or GitHub depending on `entire repo mirror use`) and records trail metadata via Entire's API; it never independently re-pushes to GitHub. So the commit reaches github.com only if the user's `origin`/`upstream` remote actually points at GitHub and a `git push` targets it directly — not through mirror content being relayed by Entire's backend.
